topics.label: Course introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces the course structure, student audience, and core learning outcomes for the cancer biology lecture series.

topics.label: Cancer as a failure of differentiation, tissue architecture, and cellular regulation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer at the cellular and tissue levels as a multistep breakdown in differentiation and three-dimensional tissue architecture, alongside the experimental models used to study these properties.

topics.label: Invasion, metastasis, and histological tumor progression
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the cellular mechanisms and histological criteria that distinguish benign from malignant tumors through local tissue invasion, dissemination pathways, and progression from precursor lesions.

topics.label: Tumor classification, nomenclature, and clinical mechanisms of disease
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics cover the standard naming conventions for different tumor types and the physiological mechanisms through which benign and malignant growths cause patient morbidity and mortality.

topics.label: Tumor incidence and comparative oncology across species
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine epidemiological patterns of tumor incidence in humans and other animal taxa, demonstrating that cancer is a fundamental vulnerability of multicellular organisms.

topics.label: Principles and clinical modalities of cancer screening
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics discuss the rationale, histological techniques, and clinical utility and limitations of screening programs designed to detect cancers at early or pre-malignant stages.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and practical reminders
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the session with a recap of the learning outcomes and reminders regarding upcoming practicals and lectures.
